items.title: How much track record does real advocacy actually need?
items.description: Simple teaching model, not a measured curve: represents the odds a senior colleague would actually advocate for you, unprompted, in a room you're not in, as a function of months of genuine, low-stakes usefulness to them. It rises slowly at first and only becomes likely after a real, sustained stretch — reflecting why this can't be compressed into a few weeks of urgent attentiveness. The default sits near Priya's own two-year mark from L3.
items.compute: const advocacyOdds = Math.round(100 * Math.pow(params.monthsOfTrackRecord / 30, 1.8)); return { advocacyOdds };

outputs.label: Odds a sponsor would advocate for you unprompted

items.title: How many real sponsors does it take to close the gap?
items.description: Simple teaching model, not a measured curve: represents how vulnerable you are to an unfair situation going unchallenged in rooms you're not in, as a function of how many genuine sponsor relationships you've built. It's highest at zero sponsors (Marcus's position in L1) and drops sharply after just one real sponsor (Priya's position), leveling off after that, since a second or third sponsor adds real but diminishing protection once one already exists.
items.compute: const vulnerability = Math.round(100 * Math.exp(-params.numSponsors * 1.1)); return { vulnerability };
